description: Japchae Sweet Potato Glass Noodles is a beloved Korean dish featuring chewy sweet potato starch noodles stir-fried with an array of colorful vegetables and often meat, all tossed in a savory soy garlic sauce. This vibrant and flavorful Korean pasta offers a delightful balance of textures and tastes, making it a popular choice for celebrations and everyday meals alike. It is a fantastic way to enjoy a wholesome and satisfying dish that is both sweet and savory.

ingredients.notes: soaked in warm water for 30 minutes
thinly sliced (optional, or use mushrooms for vegetarian)

instructions.title: Prepare the Noodles
instructions.text: Soak sweet potato glass noodles in warm water for 30 minutes until pliable. Drain and set aside. In a large pot, bring water to a boil, cook the soaked noodles for 5-7 minutes until transparent and chewy. Drain well, rinse with cold water to prevent sticking, and toss with 1 tbsp soy sauce and 1 tbsp sesame oil. This ensures flavorful, non-sticky noodles.

instructions.title: Marinate and Cook Beef (Optional)
instructions.text: If using beef, marinate thinly sliced beef with 1 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tsp sugar, 1 clove minced garlic, 1 tsp sesame oil, and a pinch of black pepper for 10 minutes. Heat 1 tbsp vegetable oil in a large wok or pan over medium-high heat. Stir-fry the marinated beef until fully cooked, then remove from the pan and set aside.

instructions.title: Prepare Vegetables Separately
instructions.text: Blanch the spinach in boiling water for 30 seconds, drain, squeeze out excess water, and season with 1 tsp soy sauce and 1 tsp sesame oil. In the same pan, add a little oil and stir-fry each vegetable separately: carrots until slightly tender, then onions until translucent, then bell peppers, and finally shiitake mushrooms until fragrant. Season each vegetable lightly with a pinch of salt if desired. Remove each vegetable from the pan as it cooks.

instructions.title: Make the Japchae Sauce
instructions.text: In a small bowl, whisk together the remaining 3 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp sugar, 2 cloves minced garlic, and 2 tbsp sesame oil. Taste and adjust sweetness or saltiness as needed. This will be the main flavoring for the Japchae.

instructions.title: Combine All Ingredients
instructions.text: In the large wok or a very large mixing bowl, combine the cooked noodles, all the stir-fried vegetables, cooked beef (if used), and the seasoned spinach. Pour the prepared sauce over everything.

instructions.title: Toss and Serve
instructions.text: Using tongs or clean hands, thoroughly toss all the ingredients together until the noodles and vegetables are evenly coated with the sauce. Continue tossing for a few minutes to ensure the flavors meld. Garnish with toasted sesame seeds and serve warm or at room temperature.

tips: For truly authentic Japchae, blanching and stir-frying vegetables separately is key. This preserves their individual textures and vibrant colors.
Do not overcook the sweet potato glass noodles; they should be chewy, not mushy. Rinsing them in cold water after boiling stops the cooking process and prevents sticking.
Japchae is often served at room temperature, making it a great dish for potlucks or meal prepping. You can store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days.
